correctness.rationale: Normalized John ellipsoid B_2^4 and candidate a+AB_2^4 imply alpha=lambda_min(A) in (0,1] (det A<=1). The primary source (Theorem 1.1, Eq.5.1) gives det A<=U1(alpha),U2(alpha) for every feasible center-excluding candidate; its rank-one matrix premise was checked structurally: bb^T<=A^2, negative fractional powers reverse Loewner order, trace differentiation and integration yield the scalar lower increment. For alpha in (0,1], all logarithmic bases are positive. Independently eliminated the unsquared U1=U2 relation to exactly P/268435456 and the D2 stationary relation to alpha^3*Q/16; rational Sturm root counts give exactly one P root in (0,1), bracketed by 0.523194 and 0.523195, and one Q root in (0,1), bracketed by 0.5165 and 0.5166. Exact rational signs and D2(1/2)=3/175>0, D2(1)<0, plus D1-positive cubic prove D1(alpha*)>0 and D2(alpha*)<0. Since f_j(e^x) are convex, log Uj(e^x) are concave; thus U1 increases throughout (0,alpha*] and U2 decreases throughout [alpha*,1]. The pointwise minimum therefore has unique global maximum at the crossing, C4=0.81623940332041060897589..., below sqrt(e)/2. The n=4 explicit cone witness gives 4*sqrt(3)/9. Finite high-precision bisection serves display only; exact resultants/root counts and analytic concavity establish the global theorem.

value.rationale: The maximum John-ellipsoid volume after a central cut is a natural invariant in fixed-dimensional convex geometry and ellipsoid cutting-plane algorithms. The general n-dependent bounds of Zhou–Zou–Liu leave concrete fixed-dimensional quality-of-cut benchmarks unevaluated; n=4 gives a genuinely active two-constraint crossing at a nontrivial algebraic alpha* (rather than a bare parameter substitution), with an exact determinant guarantee and comparison to the canonical cone. An explicit universal improvement 0.8243606... to 0.8162394... is modest but mathematically motivated, and the root-isolation/crossing geometry can guide more refined four-dimensional estimates. A full solution of the fixed-dimensional extremal problem is NOT claimed or required for an independently useful exact benchmark.
residual_risks: The improvement is quantitative and modest, not the true c4; stronger geometric inequalities may dominate this exact two-bound benchmark.
This is a specifically dimension-four calculation, not an all-n closed solution; value lies in exact low-dimensional bound and active-certificate transition.
